case_title.quote: SHIV A KUMAR @ SHIV A @ SHIV AMURTHY v. STATE OF KARNATAKA

number_of_accused.quote: The appellant has been convicted for the offences

accused_gender.quote: he has no antecedents and poses no threat to society

accused_age.correct_value: 27 at conviction (22 at time of offence, per counsel)
accused_age.quote: on the date of conviction, the age of the appellant was 27 years
accused_age.reason: Judgment gives 27 at conviction and 22 at offence; the value omits the latter.

accused_occupation.quote: the appellant, who was the driver

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on wealth or class.

previous_criminal_record.quote: this was the first offence committed by the appellant
previous_criminal_record.reason: First offence and no antecedents are noted.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Driver of the company vehicle in which the victim travelled (employee transport provider/stranger-like prior connection)
accused_victim_relationship.quote: she was informed by the appellant, who was the driver, that the vehicle operating on route no.131 was not available
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Judgment describes a connection: the accused was the company's driver who transported her.

offence_category.quote: convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376 and 302
offence_category.reason: Murder is defensible, but the case involves rape and murder; category is ambiguous.

statutory_provisions.quote: Sections 366, 376 and 302 of the Indian Penal Code

evidence_type.quote: her dead body was recovered at the instance of the appellant
evidence_type.reason: Recovery evidence and complaint are mentioned.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: The facts are such, which will shock the conscience of any Court

mitigating_circumstances.quote: he has completed B.A. degree course while in jail
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Matches counsel's points and the Trial Court's factors.

trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced the appellant to undergo rigorous imprisonment for the rest of his life

final_outcome.quote: we modify the order of sentence of the Trial Court

offence_finally_established.quote: convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376 and 302

imprisonment_type.quote: we direct that the appellant shall undergo imprisonment for life
imprisonment_type.reason: Sentence is life imprisonment with a 30-year no-release term, so 'life' fits better than fixed_term.

imprisonment_years.correct_value: null (life imprisonment; release only after 30 years)
imprisonment_years.quote: released only after he completes thirty years of actual sentence
imprisonment_years.reason: Sentence is life with a 30-year minimum, not a pure fixed term.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove the final sentence on the prosecution case and 'life cut short in a brutal manner' wording; avoid the 'accused committed' assertion.
neutral_facts.quote: The prosecution successfully established the charge of the offence of rape
neutral_facts.reason: Mostly accurate, but the last sentence asserts guilt; the age detail and the 'brutal' characterisation are judge-style.

offence_severity.correct_value: Not stated precisely; judgment only says offence is punishable with death penalty, with life imprisonment as alternative
offence_severity.quote: an offence which is punishable with death penalty
offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not set out the s.302 maximum and minimum explicitly.

physical_harm.reason: Death after rape; no injuries described.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: her dead body was recovered at the instance of the appellant

post_offence_conduct.reason: Only body recovery at his instance, which is not described as conduct.

custody_duration.quote: has undergone sentence for approximately seventeen years and two months

legal_representation.quote: K. Parameshwar, Shekhar G Devasa, Manish Tiwari

investigation_status.quote: The maternal uncle of the deceased lodged a complaint

procedural_irregularity.quote: the Trial Court could not have directed that the appellant shall not be released till the rest of his life

appeal_history.quote: The High Court, by the impugned judgment, dismissed both appeals.

prosecution_argument.quote: Constitutional Courts are not powerless to impose modified sentences

defence_argument.correct_value: Also argued mitigating facts: age 22 at offence, young wife, small child, aged parents, no antecedents, good jail conduct, B.A. completed, 17 years served.
defence_argument.quote: he has completed B.A. degree course while in jail

legal_principle_applied.quote: Constitutional Courts can always exercise the power of imposing a modified or fixed-term sentence

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Union of India v. V. Sriharan alias Murugan & Ors. 2016 (7) SCC 1 – followed

sentencing_rationale.quote: showing undue leniency in such a brutal case will adversely affect the public confidence

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: the age of the appellant was 27 years and he had a wife and small child
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Trial Court factors noted by the Court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Brutal nature of the crime; safety and security of women working night shifts; public confidence; victim's rights
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: The issue is of safety and security of women working with such companies.
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Largely right, but 'avoid undue leniency' and 'victim's rights' are considerations, not aggravating facts.

other_sentence_order.quote: released only after he completes thirty years of actual sentence
